- [FACT] Repudiation of a building contract occurs when one party evinces an intention no longer to be bound by the contract.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the information about repudiation of a building contract.
- [FACT] Key takeaways regarding repudiation of a building contract include: 
  1. Builders and/or building company directors/senior staff should engage lawyers early and stop sending correspondence by phone, letter, email, and text message.
  2. It is advised never to say phrases like “we want to terminate the contract” or “we do not want to continue with this build” as this could be considered repudiation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the key takeaways regarding repudiation of a building contract.
- [FACT] Repudiation of a contract occurs when a party shows an unwillingness or inability to perform substantial obligations under the contract, often referred to as renunciation.
- [FACT] Contract repudiation is considered a breach of contract, allowing the other party to terminate the contract and seek damages.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the definition of repudiation of a contract.
- [FACT] A party may breach a contractual provision, such as failing to pay within a specified time, which may give the innocent party the right to terminate the contract.
- [FACT] Repudiation often arises from breaches of the contract, and the innocent party may rely on common law rights to terminate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the information about whether repudiation is a breach of contract.
- [FACT] Repudiation is not the same as termination; it refers to the conduct that allows the innocent party to terminate the contract.
- [FACT] The effect of termination is to bring the contract to an end, and the innocent party may claim damages.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the distinction between repudiation and termination.
- [FACT] Accepting repudiation allows the innocent party to terminate the contract, which is deemed void at common law.
- [FACT] One cannot sue specifically for repudiation but can bring a claim for breach of contract.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges the information about what happens if one accepts repudiation.
- [FACT] There is no straightforward formula for proving a repudiatory breach; it must be considered in context.
- [FACT] If a party intends to terminate for repudiation, they should provide opportunities for the at-fault party to rectify the breach.
